sections.h2: Where to file a deed in Calhoun County
sections.html:
Calhoun County accepts land documents at one office only: the Marshall County Building, 315 West Green Street, home of the Clerk and Register of Deeds. The second county office, at 161 East Michigan Avenue in Battle Creek, handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders, so a deed taken there goes nowhere. Call the Marshall counter at 269-781-0718 if you are unsure.

The research room, used by title searchers and genealogists, is open on business days and closes at 4:45 p.m., a quarter hour before the office itself. The Marshall building also issues marriage licenses, vital records and notary commissions, so expect a mixed crowd at the counter. A drop box at the west edge of the parking lot behind the County Building takes completed documents with payment enclosed. The county also runs an online land record search and a property alert tool.

Clerks cannot give legal advice about completing a land record form, and the office stocks no blank forms. Questions go to a lawyer. The State Bar of Michigan referral line is 1-800-968-0738, and Michigan Legal Help is another free place to start.

A flat $30 buys the recording of any document, long or short. That covers deeds, mortgages, certified copies, lis pendens, timber, oil and gas leases, UCC filings, Land Division Act filings, discharges and terminations, and federal, state and employment security liens. Land record payments are taken as cash or check, nothing else.

  • Add $3 for each additional liber and page referenced on a discharge or assignment.
  • Pay $5 to the treasurer for the tax certification a warranty deed or land contract requires.
  • Copies cost $1 a page for real estate records, $2 for UCC filings, and at least $2 a page for plats.
  • Certification of a recorded instrument is $5.

The base fee comes from MCL 600.2567: $30 to enter and record a document, with $3 added for each further instrument assigned or discharged.

sections.h2: Can I record a Calhoun County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, with one carve-out. Every document type can be e-recorded except those that require a real estate transfer tax valuation affidavit. Those have to be mailed or brought to the Marshall counter. E-recording runs through a vendor: you scan and upload, the register reviews, and anything with errors comes back for correction before it is stamped and returned by electronic delivery.

Four vendors work with the county: CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. Sign up as a customer with one of them; each offers demonstrations and training. When a document needs tax certification, the system routes it to the County Treasurer's Office, so you make no separate trip for the certificate.

sections.h2: What the Marshall office checks on a deed
sections.html:
The county's posted checklist rests on MCL 565.201 and adds items that catch people who draft their own deeds.

  • Signatures in original ink, each with a typed or printed name below it that agrees with the notary block.
  • Street or post office addresses for grantees, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A Michigan acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary.
  • For any deed that names a survivor, a certified death certificate that was recorded earlier and is cited by liber and page.
  • Court orders bearing the court clerk's certification and seal.
  • A first line stating one recordable event, black type of 10 points or more on white 20-pound paper, and a 2 1/2 inch blank band above the first line of page one and 1/2 inch on the other edges.
  • The land's total value shown on the deed or in an attached valuation affidavit. The county bars the stock phrase "and other good and valuable consideration."
  • Any transfer tax exemption spelled out on the instrument, and a trust document recorded as a separate paper.

If you are selling, your closing attorney or title company normally handles this list. If you are drafting a deed yourself, run through it line by line before you drive to Marshall.

The Calhoun County Treasurer signs off. A warranty deed, a land contract, an assignment of a land contract or any deed with a warranty covenant must carry the treasurer's certification before the register accepts it, and the fee is $5. Call 269-781-0807 with questions about deed certification. When you e-record, the system forwards the paper to the treasurer for you.

The rule comes from MCL 211.135: the parcel must be free of tax liens and tax titles, and the five years of taxes before the deed date must be paid. A plain quitclaim without a warranty covenant is outside it.

An owner who has fallen behind will run into the balance at this step. Pay it off before the closing date so the recording stays on schedule. On a cash sale to a buyer who wants to close quickly, this is the one errand that can hold things up, so ask the treasurer about any balance early.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Calhoun County sale
sections.html:
Stack the county's 55 cents (MCL 207.504) on the state's $3.75 (MCL 207.525) and you get $4.30 for each $500 of value, with any remainder counted as one more block. A fraction of a block counts as a whole one, so a $162,800 home, the typical owner-occupied value here, becomes 326 blocks instead of 325.6.

Owners selling a troubled property care most about three exemptions. A deed in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure on any mortgage is exempt under the state act, while the county act covers only government-backed loans. A court order that sets no price escapes both taxes. A transfer to a child or grandchild appears on the state list in MCL 207.526. Whatever you claim should be written on the instrument.

sections.h2: Calhoun County housing at a glance
sections.html: Calhoun County has about 133,408 residents and 59,808 housing units, centered on Battle Creek, the largest city, and Marshall, the county seat. Owners live in 72.7% of homes. The typical owner-occupied home is worth $162,800, typical gross rent is $968, and the county's 53,333 households earn a median $63,177. At that typical value a sale triggers roughly $1,400 of transfer tax, and the rates are the same in every Michigan county.

faqs.q: What will I owe the Calhoun County recorder for a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document, paid in cash or by check. A discharge or assignment adds $3 per additional liber and page it references, and a warranty deed needs the $5 treasurer tax certification as well.

faqs.q: Will the Battle Creek office record my deed?
faqs.a: No. Land documents are filed only at the Marshall office, 315 West Green Street. Battle Creek handles circuit court filings and personal protection orders.

faqs.q: Is e-recording available for Calhoun County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes, through CSC, ePN, Indecomm and Simplifile. A document with a transfer tax valuation affidavit is the exception and must be mailed or delivered to Marshall.

faqs.q: What commonly gets a Calhoun County deed returned?
faqs.a: Typical reasons are a missing grantee address, no drafter name, signer names that disagree with the acknowledgment, no stated property value, and margins or type size outside the statute. The office returns rejected paper with the reasons checked off.

faqs.q: Who pays the Calhoun County transfer tax in a sale?
faqs.a: The statutes tax the written instrument and leave payment to the parties, so the purchase agreement governs. A $162,800 sale carries $1,401.80 in combined county and state tax.
